meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_61_packages.json, all reference===61 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_61.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, נִקְרֵאת, הַיְנוּ) were considered as flagged additions. Concepts already captured in existing dataset edges (reference===61, type==='bechina') are excluded.

additions.reason: The Rebbe states explicitly in Section ו: 'הַשֵּׂכֶל נִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ' — the intellect IS called 'holy' (קֹדֶשׁ). This is a direct נִקְרָא bechina statement. The node שֵׂכֶל is absent from the dataset for Torah #61, yet it plays a pivotal structural role: the Rebbe explains that all sweetening of judgments comes through the שֵׂכֶל, which is the root of all דינים and is named 'קֹדֶשׁ.' This establishes שֵׂכֶל as a bechina of קֹדֶשׁ (and by extension, of קָדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים and שֵֹּכֶל הָעֶלְיוֹן already in Package 1). The missing edge: שֵׂכֶל ↔ קֹדֶשׁ (ref. 61, bechina). A second edge may also be flagged: שֵׂכֶל ↔ שֵֹּכֶל הָעֶלְיוֹן (as the general intellect IS the supreme intellect at its root), though this would require careful canonical judgment.
additions.source_quote: כִּי כָּל הַמְתָּקוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַצִּמְצוּמִים וְהַדִּינִים הוּא עַל-יְדֵי הַשֵּׂכֶל... וְהַשֵּׂכֶל נִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ

additions.reason: Section ג contains two explicit נִקְרֵאת (= 'is called') bechina statements about the נְשָׁמָה that are absent from the dataset for Torah #61: (1) 'הַנְּשָׁמָה נִקְרֵאת שָׁמַיִם' — the soul is called 'heavens' because it is the collective governor of all the celestial spheres; (2) 'הַנְּשָׁמָה נִקְרֵאת גַּלְגַּלְתָּא, עַל שֵׁם גַּלְגַּלֵּי הָרָקִיעַ שֶׁמִּתְנַהֲגִים עַל יָדָהּ' — the soul is called 'gulgalta' (skull/sphere-cluster) because the celestial spheres are governed through it. The soul in Torah #61 plays the role of the שֵׂכֶל הַכּוֹלֵל — the all-encompassing intellect that includes and governs all the particular celestial intelligences (שִׂכְלִיִּים / מַלְאָכִים). This places נְשָׁמָה as a bechina of שָׁמַיִם and of גַּלְגַּלְתָּא, both missing from the Torah #61 dataset. Additionally, the text states 'שֵׂכֶל הַכּוֹלֵל, שֶׁהִיא הַנְּשָׁמָה' — reinforcing that נְשָׁמָה = שֵׂכֶל הַכּוֹלֵל, linking it to Package 1's domain of supernal intellect.

additions.reason: Section ב contains an explicit bechina statement: 'הַסְּמִיכָה שֶׁסּוֹמְכִין אֶת הָרַב, וְהַכְּתָב, הֵם מִבְּחִינָה אַחַת. כִּי הַסְּמִיכָה בְּיָדַיִם... וְהוּא בְּחִינַת הַכְּתָב, בְּחִינַת יָד כּוֹתֶבֶת.' Ordination (סְמִיכָה) IS a bechina of writing (כְּתָב): both are the transmission of the light of the supernal intellect through the hand. Furthermore, the verse quoted: 'בִּכְתַב בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִכָּתֵבוּ – זֶה סְמִיכָה' (Section ג, citing the Talmud Ketubot 112) explicitly equates the scriptural verse about writing/inscription with ordination. The node סְמִיכָה is absent from the Torah #61 dataset and should be added as a bechina of כְּתָב. Its polarity is good (it describes the proper ordination of a worthy sage, which brings light to the written tradition). Since it defines the boundary between the holy and the corrupt rabbi (Section ב), it belongs with Package 2 (faith in sages/true judgment) as the institutional act that validates the chain of authority.

additions.reason: The text contains multiple explicit bechina statements establishing כְּתָב as a distinct conceptual node: (1) 'הַסְּמִיכָה... וְהוּא בְּחִינַת הַכְּתָב' (ordination = writing); (2) 'הַכְּתָב הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִבְּחִינַת חָכְמָה' (writing IS from the aspect of wisdom); (3) 'הַכְּתָב הוּא בְּחִינַת אוֹתִיּוֹת מַחְכִּימוֹת' (writing IS the wisdom-letters). The concept כְּתָב ידינו (our holy script/writing) is a central theme of Sections ב-ג: it is the tangible expression of the holy chain of transmission (ordination → wisdom → writing → sanctification of the air → ability to receive great souls). Its absence from the Torah #61 bechina dataset is a significant gap. It belongs in Package 2 as the written manifestation of the faith-in-sages transmission chain.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַכְּתָב הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִבְּחִינַת חָכְמָה, כִּי אוֹתִיּוֹת הַכְּתָב, בָּהֶם נִבְרְאוּ כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת

additions.reason: Section א contains the explicit bechina: 'נִדּוֹן בִּיגִיעַת בָּשָׂר, הַיְנוּ בְּמוֹתָרוֹת' — the verse's phrase 'יְגִיעַת בָּשָׂר' (toil of the flesh = the physical excess described in Kohelet 12:12 'וְלַהַג הַרְבֵּה יְגִיעַת בָּשָׂר') IS identified by the Rebbe as בְּחִינַת מוֹתָרוֹת. This is a direct 'הַיְנוּ' bechina statement equating the scriptural phrase with the Torah #61 concept of excess-waste. The node יְגִיעַת בָּשָׂר is absent from the dataset but is an alias/bechina of מוֹתָרוֹת (Package 3) and should be added as a bechina pair.
additions.source_quote: נִדּוֹן בִּיגִיעַת בָּשָׂר, הַיְנוּ בְּמוֹתָרוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין כא): הַלּוֹעֵג עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים נִדּוֹן בְּצוֹאָה רוֹתַחַת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וְלַהַג הַרְבֵּה יְגִיעַת בָּשָׂר

additions.reason: Section ח (the zoharic conclusion) contains: 'הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל... דְּלֵית רוּחֵהּ רוּחָא דְּקִיּוּמָא, הַיְנוּ רוּחַ חָכְמָה; וְלָא הֲוָה מְהֵימָנָא, הַיְנוּ אֱמוּנַת חֲכָמִים.' The gossip/slanderer IS identified (הַיְנוּ) as the one who lacks רוּחַ חָכְמָה AND lacks אֱמוּנַת חֲכָמִים. This is a double bechina: the הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל IS the person who has damaged אֱמוּנַת חֲכָמִים — the essential quality of Package 3's evil domain. The הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל is the concrete human embodiment of the evil described throughout Torah #61 (slander = damaged faith in sages = the root of the מוֹתָרוֹת-משפט מעקל cascade). Missing from dataset.

additions.reason: Section ח states: 'מְגַלֶּה סוֹד, זֶה בְּחִינַת בִּטּוּל כְּתַב יָדֵנוּ.' 'Revealing the secret' (the gossip/reckless disclosure) IS a bechina of the nullification of our holy writing. This is explicit (זֶה = בְּחִינַת) bechina language. The node מְגַלֶּה סוֹד is the act of betraying the transmitted wisdom; it IS defined as the undermining of כְּתַב יָדֵנוּ. Since כְּתָב belongs to Package 2 (the positive chain of transmission), מְגַלֶּה סוֹד (as its negation/evil mirror) belongs at the boundary between Package 2 and Package 3. It is most naturally placed with Package 3 (evil domain) as the evil counterpart to כְּתָב and אֱמוּנַת חֲכָמִים. (Note: 'negative polarity concept adjacent to Package 2' — flagged here under Package 2 for reviewer awareness, but recommended for Package 3 placement.)
additions.source_quote: מְגַלֶּה סוֹד, זֶה בְּחִינַת בִּטּוּל כְּתַב יָדֵנוּ, שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹר הַשֵּׂכֶל מִידֵי הַסְּמִיכָה כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: Section ב contains: 'כִּי בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל יוֹשְׁבִין שָׁם מִכְּבָר, אֲפִלּוּ בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ, הוּא בְּחִינַת קְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ-יִשְׂרָאֵל, בְּחִינַת (יְחֶזְקֵאל יא): מִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט.' The long-established settlements of Israel — even in the diaspora — ARE a bechina of 'a small sanctuary' (מִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט). This is an explicit biblical phrase used as a bechina term. It belongs to Package 1 because it is connected to the sanctification of the air (אֲוִירָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל) that enables great souls (Package 1's soul-domain) and is produced through the proper transmission of wisdom via כְּתַב יָדֵנוּ. Missing from Torah #61 dataset.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Mentioned as a historical example of learning from מותרות (Section א). The Rebbe says his learning was 'מבחינת עצירות, בחינת מותרות' — but דואג himself is a named instance, not a bechina-concept being equated. Excluded per framework: named historical figures used as examples, not bechina declarations of their essential nature.

Section ג: 'גּוּף, בִּבְחִינוֹת פְּרִי הָאָרֶץ, בְּחִינוֹת אֲוִירָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.' This IS bechina language — the body of the great soul must be formed from 'fruit of the earth' (= אוירא דארץ ישראל). However, פְּרִי הָאָרֶץ is used here as a verse citation (Isaiah 4:2), not as a standalone concept-node that the Rebbe develops independently. The essential content is captured through the אֲוִירָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל concept (which feeds into Package 1's soul-domain). Marginal case — flagged but not recommended for addition without further review.

Section ג describes the celestial spheres (גַּלְגַּלִּים) governed by intelligences (שִׂכְלִיִּים = מַלְאָכִים). These are part of the cosmological background of the teaching, not explicitly established as bechina-nodes in their own right. The text describes their function (eitza: the intelligences govern the spheres) rather than declaring them bechina-equivalences. Excluded.

Section ז: 'כִּי רֹאשׁ-הַשָּׁנָה הוּא יוֹמָא דְּדִינָא שֶׁל כָּל הַשָּׁנָה.' This is a definitional statement about the halakhic character of ראש השנה (it is the day of judgment), not a bechina establishing an unexpected parallel. Excluded.

Section ח describes שמחה as the result of souls being included in the tzaddik ('אוֹר צַדִּיקִים יִשְׂמָח'). However, the edge referencing שמחה in the dataset (edge 2973: 'שנכללים יחד כל הנפשות' → נַעֲשֶׂה שִׂמְחָה) is classified as eitza, not bechina — joy is the RESULT of the inclusion, not a bechina-parallel of it. Correctly classified; not a gap.

Mentioned repeatedly (Sections ב-ג) as a bechina of the air sanctified by Israel's presence and by the holy script. A significant bechina concept that may warrant addition, but is tightly bound to the 'מקדש מעט / כתב' cluster already flagged as additions. Cross-referenced with the מקדש מעט entry above. Recommend consolidating into a single addition edge: אֲוִירָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל ↔ מִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט if added.
